rules.sentence: Echocardiography shows signs of pulmonary hypertension, such as elevated pulmonary arterial systolic pressure (PASP), right ventricular strain/dilation, and right ventricular dysfunction.
Spirometry typically shows normal values, though mild restrictive defects may be seen.[44]
Echocardiography will also be useful to exclude left-sided heart disease as a cause of pulmonary edema.
Ventilation and perfusion scanning (V/Q scanning) is typically performed in the workup of patients with suspected PAH.
It is of poor utility in diagnosing PVOD because it is usually normal or leads to a misdiagnosis of CTEPH.
However, a recent study demonstrated that the prevalence of mismatched perfusion defects from V/Q Scanning in PVOD was low and was not significantly different from PAH (7.1% vs. 10%, p>0.05).
Therefore it is not a useful test for differentiating PVOD from PAH.[46]
